content.thinking: The page is dark, and it's showing the Hebrew question "where and how is cheapest to invest in an index". The Tel Aviv 125 index is already selected, with 10,000 as the sum today and 500 monthly, so I'll keep going.

The narration is in Hebrew with some English, so the rewrite should be in Hebrew. The content: the user put in 70,000, the cheaper option comes to 86,045 after 10 years in today's money, which is the headline figure; the other box shows a minus 1,030 that Claude doesn't want; Claude has heard of Psagot but it isn't the user's bank; and the fund is an index tracker, the A-B-I tracker of the TA-125 index.

Claude writes: הסכום שהפקדתם הוא 70,000, והמספר הגדול הוא 86,045 ש"ח בכסף של היום, אחרי 10 שנים ואחרי דמי ניהול ומס. התיבה השנייה עם המינוס 1,030 איננה הבחירה שאני רוצה, וקרן המחקה של אי.בי.אי על ת"א 125 היא המוצר שאבדוק הלאה.

Your bank pays less than פסגות at the top of the list (לאומי 82,968, הפועלים 81,052, דיסקונט 79,491, מזרחי טפחות 77,294), a gap of a few thousand. The coloured bars and the 1,049 versus 4,506 figures are still unclear to me, so I'll check what they measure next.

The colour key and the fund details are on the page, but the cheapest option appears to be פסגות with the אי.בי.אי. מחקה ת"א 125 fund, which would leave about 86,000 ₪ after ten years from 70,000 ₪ invested, versus roughly 81,000–83,000 ₪ at my own bank. I'm not doing anything until we've talked it through.

input.answer: According to the page, the cheapest is an account at פסגות with the fund "אי.בי.אי. מחקה (4A) ת"א 125". With 10,000 now and 500 a month, I'd put in 70,000 and have about 86,045 ₪ after ten years. At the big banks it would be about 81,000–83,000. I'm not acting on it myself; I'll ask my son first, because of the minus signs and the words I don't understand.

stuck.why: "להשקיע במדד": to me מדד is the price index from the news, and the buttons are full of English letters (MSCI, S&P 500). I nearly left.
"−1,030 ₪ לעומת הבחירה שלכם" with a minus sign. I backed away from that option without really understanding it.
"−0.04% בשנה · שנה אחת" has a minus on the fund marked as the choice. I didn't know whether it means it lost money, and it worried me.
The colour key is only at the bottom, after all the rows. I had to go back up to match colours to bars, and the oranges and yellows look alike.
